prompt: When the temperature of the entire universe was between 0 and 100 degrees Celsius, what fraction of the size of the universe was the size of the universe now?
judge_reasoning: Candidate [1] is the only response that attempts to directly answer the question with a fraction of the universe’s current size (about 1–2%), which—while not derived with full rigor—matches the right order of magnitude for 0–100°C (roughly 0.7–1% in linear scale factor). Candidate [3] performs a scale-factor calculation but uses the wrong temperature input (1000°C rather than 0–100°C), yielding a clearly mismatched fraction. Candidates [2] and [4] do not provide the requested fraction of the universe’s size at 0–100°C, instead discussing unrelated temperature-era context and processes without the needed ratio.
